title: llm-routing-prefetch-poc-scratchpad
content:
Context / why: trying to reduce tail latency for multi-turn chat by prefetching KV cache and routing requests to warmed model variants when possible. Want a small POC to validate latency wins + cost delta and catch any correctness/regression risk.

Problem statement:  multi-turn sessions often suffer repeated cold KV loads and context re-encoding; users with sticky sessions see token-level latency spikes. Can we cheaply prefetch KV for popular prompts or recent prefixes and route low-risk requests to a warmed short-context variant?

Goals (success criteria):
- 95th pct latency reduction for multi-turn sessions by >= 20% on p50/p95 for sample workload (internal chat app).
- End-to-end token cost change within +-10% or net reduction.
- No >2% increase in generation regressions on quality eval set (LLM-qa + conversation-coherence).

High-level approach (POC):
- Build lightweight prefetcher service that monitors recent prefixes and issues async KV load to target model instances (warmed pool).
- Add routing rule: if session score (popularity + recency heuristic) >= threshold, route to warmed pool; otherwise fallback to normal cold path.
- Instrument metrics: per-request cache-hit, KV-prefetch-latency, model-variant-switches, cost-per-token.

User stories / flows (rough):
- As an app dev, I want my chat users to see more consistent latency for long conversations so UX feels snappier.
- As infra, I want a knob to control prefetch aggressiveness and budget so ops can cap cost.

Open questions / risks (TODOs):
- How much additional memory for kv cache per worker? need infra cost estimate.
- Correctness: prefetch might load wrong KV if session mutated rapidly; need guardrails and TTL.
- Failure modes: warmed pool saturated -> fallback latency spike. Add circuit-breaker.
- Security / privacy: ensure prefetch respects tenant data isolation and KMS boundaries.

Experiment plan:
- Start with narrow cohort (internal chat team) 5% traffic. Run A/B with metric collection for 2 weeks.
- Metrics: p50/p95 generation latency, end-to-end request latency, tokens per request, cost estimate, quality regressions.

Implementation notes / sketch:
- Prefetcher component watches prefix popularity table (redis or in-memory LRU), triggers async load via existing KV API (reuse /kv-prefetch endpoint).
- Warmed pool = small dedicated pool of workers with preloaded KV and pinning policy for short TTL (30s).
- Routing decision in fronting layer: evaluate session score, route header X-Model-Variant: warmed if eligible.

Next steps (immediate):
- Sync with Raja (serving runtime) for warmed pool feasibility and memory estimates.
- Draft small infra cost calc + add to JIRA-INFR-482.
- Create proto instrumentation dashboard in observability (p50/p95 + cache-hit).

Notes to self: keep PRD minimal for now; goal is a quick, measurable POC. Capture lessons and decide whether to bake into routing playbook or Optimize product later.

Partial todo list:
- [ ] Quick spike: measure cold vs warmed token latencies on toy prefix set (Sophia)
- [ ] Infra estimate: memory, extra workers, ops knobs (Raja)
